notes: §1985:IX.1.3.4 gives the implementor one class of I-O status for an indexed file: "I-O Status = 9x. An implementor-defined condition exists. This condition must not duplicate any condition specified for the I-O status values 00 through 49. The value of x is defined by the implementor." The runtime's status values are the constants of FileStatus.cs, and two are 9x: 90 (LinageValueViolation), which only a sequential file with a LINAGE clause can answer, and 91 (CharacterWithoutByteImage), the one an indexed file reaches: KeyedConnector.RecordRulesFailure, asked by every indexed WRITE and REWRITE after the open-mode rule (48, 49), REWRITE's 43 and the record size rule (44) and before any key rule, answers it when FileConnector.RecordHasCharacterWithoutByteImage finds a character the file's coded character set cannot hold (above U+00FF with no CODE-SET clause, FileCharacterSet.HasCharacterWithoutByteImage). No status of 00 through 49 names that condition (30 is the permanent error with "no further information"), and every condition the 1985 list does name keeps its own value, so nothing is duplicated; x is documented in docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-110. No member reads the edition to choose 91, so --std 85 reaches it as written. The edition arm is the other way round: the later editions' statuses above 49 are not produced at 85 (FileConnector.SharingFacilityInEffect is false, so FileRegistry.SharedOpenAttempt asks no Table 19 arbitration and ImplementorDefaultSharing restricts no other connector: no 61, and with no LOCK MODE clause no 5x), which leaves 9x the only class outside the 1985 list. Probed at --std 85 on an indexed file: a WRITE and a REWRITE of a record holding U+20AC answer 91 and run the USE procedure, not the INVALID KEY phrase, and the file keeps the earlier record; the same WRITE on a file open INPUT answers 48; a second connector on the same physical file opens I-O and OUTPUT with 00 and its READ, REWRITE and the first connector's DELETE answer 00. The witness shows a duplicate prime key reported as 22, the standard's own value, and never as a 9x.

next.reason: The bar on the implementor's 9x conditions is widened. 1985: 'This condition must not duplicate any condition specified for the I-O status values 00 through 49' (§1985:IX.1.3.4). 2023: 'This condition shall not duplicate any other condition specified by another I-O status value' (§2023:9.1.13.11 GR1), which now also excludes the 5x, 6x and 7x conditions. A 1985 program reaches these: with no SHARING phrase or clause 'the implementor defines the sharing mode in which the file is opened' (§2023:9.1.15), and an OPEN that conflicts with another file connector is status 61 (§2023:9.1.13.9 GR1), a condition a 1985 implementor could report as 9x. The value of x stays implementor-defined (§2023:A.1 110).
